insights.headline: Yields and the dollar keep the lid on gold; festive demand heads into its priciest Dhanteras
insights.summary: Gold held just above $4,130-$4,160 overnight as a strong dollar and 10-year Treasury yields near 5.35% offset relief from fading October Fed-hike bets. The LBMA 2026 conference heard that gold's resilience despite surging yields signals a debasement trade on unsustainable government debt, while Heraeus flagged the break of $4,250 support and weak July silver output from Mexico. Silver's fate hinges on $59.69 support. At home, the GST Council meets Oct 8 on nominated-agency import taxation and the RBI decides on rates Oct 7 — ahead of the costliest Dhanteras on record.
points: Gold is caught between fading October Fed-hike bets (22%) and multi-decade-high yields plus a yearly-high dollar, pinned near $4,130-$4,160.
The LBMA 2026 conference framed gold's resilience as a 'debasement trade' — investors fearing government debt more than craving bond income.
Silver sits at a technical crossroads around $59.69; Deutsche Bank's 2027-surplus call and soft Mexico output pull in opposite directions.
India: GST Council meets Oct 8 on taxing nominated-agency gold imports; the RBI's Oct 7 decision could move the rupee and domestic prices.
First Dhanteras under the 15% import duty with gold near Rs 1.5 lakh per 10g; jewellers still expect strong festive buying of lighter pieces.

trending.title: Yields and the dollar rule, Fed-hike bets fade
trending.summary: Weak September payrolls cut October Fed-hike odds to 22%, but a yearly-high dollar and 10-year yields above 5.3% are pinning gold near $4,130-$4,160.

trending.title: Silver's fork in the road
trending.summary: Spot silver must hold $59.69 for a recovery; Deutsche Bank sees a 2027 surplus while Heraeus notes weak July output from Mexico, the top producer.

trending.title: Tax, duty and rate decisions at home
trending.summary: The GST Council meets Oct 8 on taxing nominated-agency gold imports, and the RBI's Oct 7 rate decision could move the rupee — just as the priciest Dhanteras ever arrives.

trending.title: LBMA: the debasement thesis
trending.summary: At the LBMA's annual conference, panellists argued gold's resilience despite surging yields shows investors are pricing in government-debt debasement.

items.title: LBMA 2026: Gold is sending a message as debt fears fuel the debasement trade
items.summary: Market experts at the LBMA's annual Global Precious Metals Conference said gold's resilience despite soaring bond yields is itself a message: investors are pricing in unsustainable government debt and the erosion of fiat currencies.
points: Nippon India MF's Vikram Dhawan: global debt rising by trillions yearly leaves governments with financial repression — higher inflation, capped borrowing costs.
TRS of Texas's Shayne McGuire: investors increasingly worry growing debt will erode the value of money, reviving the debasement motive for gold.
The panel, moderated by MKS PAMP's Nicky Shiels, argued the old rulebook — surging yields kill gold — no longer holds.

items.title: Gold imports by nominated agencies may come under GST as Council weighs tax parity
items.summary: The GST Council will meet on October 8 to consider bringing gold imports by nominated agencies such as MMTC and STC under GST, aligning their tax treatment with imports routed through banks. Currently only banks pay 3% GST on gold imports.

items.title: Gold price suffers under oil, yield pressures, Mexico's silver production weakens in July – Heraeus
items.summary: Gold broke through $4,250/oz support last week as multi-decade-high bond yields, a stronger dollar and Brent near $100 overwhelmed buying interest, Heraeus analysts wrote, leaving the year-to-date lows near $4,000 as next support. They also flagged weak July silver output in Mexico, the world's largest producer.
points: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5.3%, its highest since 2002, lifting the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold.
Brent near $100 a barrel is reinforcing fears that energy costs keep inflation elevated and policy tight for longer.
For silver, Mexico — the world's largest producer — posted weak July output, a supply-side counterpoint to demand-weakness calls.

items.title: Gold gains as October Fed rate hike prospects fade
items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.4% to $4,158 an ounce on Monday after September's weak US jobs report slashed October Fed hike expectations. Payrolls rose just 29,000 against 90,000 expected, with prior months revised down; markets now see a 22% chance of an October hike, down from 64% a week ago. Silver gained 1.7% to $61.40.

items.title: Gold (XAUUSD), Silver, Platinum Forecasts – Gold Retreats As Dollar Tests Yearly Highs
items.summary: Gold slipped as the dollar tested yearly highs and Treasury yields kept climbing — 2-year notes above 4.85% and the 10-year near 5.35% — with the ISM services report keeping the US economy looking resilient, analyst Vladimir Zernov wrote. A decisive break below the $4,160-$4,180 support zone would open the way toward $4,000-$4,020.

items.title: Silver (XAG/USD) Price Forecast: $59.69 Support Holds Key to Recovery
items.summary: Spot silver is at a decision point around $59.69, analyst Bruce Powers wrote: a sustained break below turns the near-term outlook bearish, while a rally above last week's $64.11 high would signal buyers regaining control. A bearish 20/50-day moving-average crossover points to weakening momentum.

items.title: Gold falls nearly 1%, silver gains on MCX: What is driving bullion prices
items.summary: MCX gold futures slipped about 1% — Rs 1,020 per 10g — to Rs 1.49 lakh as the US dollar climbed to an 18-month high of 102.37 and Treasury yields stayed elevated, while silver rose 0.54% (Rs 1,223/kg) to Rs 2.27 lakh per kg; international spot gold held steady near $4,163.50 an ounce.

items.title: Rupee edges higher as traders await RBI policy decision on rates
items.summary: The rupee edged higher as traders positioned ahead of the RBI's monetary policy decision due October 7. Markets are split on whether the central bank will hold the repo rate at 5.25% or deliver its first hike since February 2023, with inflation above target for a third straight month.

items.title: Silver shortage could flip to surplus in 2027: Deutsche
items.summary: Deutsche Bank says silver's physical shortage could flip to surplus as early as 2027 on rising inventories and weaker industrial demand. London's freely available vault supply is up 70% since October 2025, while solar makers cut silver use via thinner contacts and cheaper pastes, metals head Daniel Ghali notes. He expects spot silver to average $70/oz by Q2 2027.

items.title: Gold, silver lose lustre in September
items.summary: Both precious metals posted negative September returns as a stronger dollar and US rate-hike expectations dented sentiment: Comex gold fell 6.8% to $4,189.1 an ounce and Comex silver 9.6% to $60.75. On MCX, gold dropped 4.1% to Rs 1,49,092 per 10 grams and silver 6.8% to Rs 2,23,740 per kg.

items.title: Festive season outlook: Jewellers expect strong buying despite changing consumer patterns
items.summary: CNBC-TV18 reports jewellers expect strong festive and wedding-season buying even as high gold prices change how consumers buy: lighter, lower-carat, versatile pieces within defined budgets, traction for old-gold exchange, and more room for diamonds. CRISIL sees 20-25% revenue growth for organised retailers this fiscal.

items.title: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, PC Jeweller shares shine - Why jewellery stocks are glittering? Expert decodes rally
items.summary: Shares of Indian jewellery retailers rallied on Monday on hopes of strong festive-season sales. Kalyan Jewellers led with a 4.5% gain while Titan and PC Jeweller rose about 1.5%. Bonanza analyst Abhinav Tiwari said the market is positioning ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali.
